question: A 69-year-old man undergoes modified radical neck dissection for an oropharyngeal tumor. During the procedure, he requires multiple blood transfusions. Four hours after the surgery, examination shows that the right and left pupils do not constrict when a light is shone into the left eye. When light is shone into the right eye, both pupils constrict. Fundoscopic examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely location of the lesion?
analysis: The patient is presenting with a classic finding of a relative afferent pupillary defect (RAPD), also known as a Marcus Gunn pupil. This indicates a lesion affecting the afferent pathway of the pupillary light reflex. Given the clinical presentation of unilateral lack of pupillary constriction when light is shone into the left eye, but constriction when light is shone into the right eye, the most likely location of the lesion is the optic nerve on the left side.
